title: Table Nine Is Missing
summary: Minutes before supper, Mina discovers a table-shaped hole in her family diner. A trail of flour, green footprints, and borrowed flowers leads her around the block to the one guest who could never miss Table Nine.
coverAlt: Under the large cream title Table Nine Is Missing, Mina searches the checkerboard diner floor with a magnifying glass. Gus peers over a red booth, empty red chairs surround a patch of floor, and a tuxedo cat watches by a red cart wheel.
style: Vibrant mid-century gouache and halftone cartoons in coral, cobalt, marigold and teal.

pages.alt: Mina carries a steaming tureen past the red diner booths. Four chairs surround an empty patch of checkerboard floor. She kneels to look through the space where Table Nine should stand.
pages.transcript:
Mina: Six bowls, six spoons. Gus, where do I put the soup?
Gus: On Nine, of course.
Mina: Then tonight we’re serving air.

pages.alt: Mina crouches over footprints in the flour. A white trail and a red wheel track wind across the checkerboard floor. A puff of flour makes her sneeze near the back door.
pages.transcript:
Mina: Four feet. No scratches. Someone lifted it.
Gus: That’s flour. I’d know our dumplings anywhere.
Mina: Bread flour. Your dumplings never make me sneeze.

pages.alt: Nella the baker steadies her bread, then remembers rolling the star-topped table along on her red bread cart. Her knocking demonstration reminds Mina of the table’s wobbly leg.
pages.transcript:
Nella: My cart? Yes. I gave Nine a lift.
Nella: That table knocked at every crack in the pavement.
Mina: Our wobbly leg! It went to Jo’s.

pages.alt: Jo the bicycle mechanic remembers treating Table Nine like a patient. Four fresh green rubber feet now protect its chrome legs. Green tracks lead through the workshop door.
pages.transcript:
Jo, remembering: Did I see a table? I treated a patient.
Jo, remembering: Four new feet. No more knocking.
Mina: And very fresh paint.

pages.alt: Mina follows green prints past a pigeon to Inez’s flower shop. The florist ties red zinnias in bright blue twine, with one length trailing out the door.
pages.transcript:
Mina: Either Nine went this way…
Mina: …or your pigeon grew three extra feet.
Inez: I only dressed the table. Ask whoever took my string.

pages.alt: Mina chases a tuxedo cat tugging the twine up a set of steps. The trail ends at a flowerpot. Below the railing, a different clue makes three knocks.
pages.transcript:
Mina: Stop! You’re attached to my best clue!
Mina: I don’t suppose you carried a table up here.
From below: Knock. Knock. KNOCK.

pages.alt: Through the alley Mina spots a red cart wheel. She and Gus slip past striped washing and discover the cobalt star table wedged sideways in a stone arch.
pages.transcript:
Mina: Nine? Your new feet aren’t supposed to knock.
Gus: Follow the sound. I’ll follow the smell.
Mina: Found you.

pages.alt: Nella and Jo struggle to push and pull the table through the arch while Inez holds the flowers. Its new green feet grip the walls. Mina stops everyone to inspect the underside.
pages.transcript:
Nella: We wanted to get it back before you noticed.
Jo: My feet work a little too well.
Mina: Nobody push. Nine has a trick.

pages.alt: Mina finds the two brass catches under the table. She and Gus separate the blue top from its chrome frame, and the neighbors carry both pieces through the arch.
pages.transcript:
Mina: One catch for each thumb. Gus taught me.
Gus: That’s how we got it through our door in 1964.
Inez: We brought four strong backs. Should’ve brought two thumbs.

pages.alt: The repaired table stands in a garden courtyard. Aunt Dot appears in a doorway wearing an enormous lavender boot and carries a wooden spoon. Mina recognizes her missing dinner guest.
pages.transcript:
Mina: So why does my table need a garden?
Aunt Dot: Because my left foot refuses to go to supper.
Mina: Aunt Dot! You could have called me.

pages.alt: Aunt Dot reminds Gus of a message. He remembers carrying a sugar bowl from the diner. A folded blue note has stuck to the bottom, and Mina peels it free.
pages.transcript:
Aunt Dot: I sent a note. Under the sugar bowl.
Gus: I carried that bowl all afternoon.
Gus: Best-kept secret on the block.

pages.alt: Dot’s invitation pictures the table, a steaming pot, and the garden. Her star-shaped cutter fits the tabletop decoration. Neighbors begin arriving at the arch with empty bowls.
pages.transcript:
Mina: “If I can’t get to Nine, could Nine come to me?”
Aunt Dot: I put that star there so any kid could find our table.
Mina: Looks like it still works.

pages.alt: Mina counts the guests and sees that four chairs will never suffice. Nella adds her bread cart, Jo levels it, and Inez unrolls a checked cloth across the neighbors’ extra tables.
pages.transcript:
Mina: Four chairs. Sixteen neighbors. One very small Nine.
Mina: Nella, line up your cart. Jo, keep it level.
Inez: What goes well with a long table? A very long cloth.

pages.alt: A winding line of mismatched tables fills the courtyard at sunset. A row of hands passes bowls along the table, and Mina smiles into hers. The tuxedo cat noses a crumb beneath the chrome legs.
pages.transcript:
Gus: Soup for Table Nine!
Aunt Dot: You solved the mystery. First dumpling is yours.
Mina: Listen. Not a single knock.

pages.alt: Next evening a child asks about the empty corner. Mina points through the diner door toward the occupied star table. She carries soup to a courtyard of neighbors and a cat with its own saucer.
pages.transcript:
New customer: Is your table missing?
Mina: Nope. It’s got a reservation.
Aunt Dot: Pull up a chair. Nine always has room.
